anatomy.name: Root
anatomy.notes: Native <dialog>. Opened with showModal() (modal) or show() (nonModal) when open turns true; closed with close(). Named by Title (aria-labelledby), described by Description when set (aria-describedby). The surface itself: no inner wrapper.

anatomy.name: Backdrop
anatomy.notRendered: A pseudo-element of the modal dialog: it has no DOM node to carry data-part.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.notes: tabIndex -1: the default focus target on open, never a Tab stop.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.notes: Holds Description, then the children. Scrolls on its own when the content is taller than the viewport, so Header and Actions stay in view.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.notes: Sits space.stack.lg below the part above it, more than the space.stack.md between the other parts, so the actions read as a separate group.

figma.note: Figma draws the open dialog only.
Native slot (layer Children), paired with Has children (default false).
Native slot, paired with Has actions (default false); preferred instances Button, TextLink.
Placement, not appearance: Figma draws the modal dialog.

constraints.reason: Dialog is controlled only. Without onOpenChange, Escape and the Close button cannot close it.

states.name: open
states.notes: showModal() or show(); focus moves in.

states.name: nonModal
states.notes: Opened with show(): sits in the page flow, no Backdrop, the page stays interactive.

accessibility.notes: Built on the native <dialog>. Modal (default): showModal() makes everything outside the dialog inert, which keeps keyboard, pointer and screen-reader focus inside; the browser sets aria-modal. Focus on open: the first [data-autofocus] descendant, otherwise Title (tabIndex -1). Focus on close: back to the element focused before opening, only when it is still connected and focus is still inside the dialog or on the body, so a consumer can move focus elsewhere in onOpenChange. Inertness and the top layer are browser behaviour that jsdom does not emulate: the a11y test covers focus, naming and Escape; inertness is checked in the browser at the visual checkpoint.
ariaAttributes: aria-describedby (Root → Description id, when description is set)
aria-modal (set by the browser for showModal())
aria-label="Close" on the icon-only Close button

keyboardInteractions.action: Calls onOpenChange(false). Modal: through the native cancel event, whose default is prevented so the open prop stays the source of truth. Non-modal: through keydown on the dialog.
Moves through the dialog's focusable elements. Modal: past the last one focus goes to the browser's own controls, then back to the first; the page behind is inert. Non-modal: continues into the page.

box-sizing.reason: Padding and border count inside the width token.

padding-inline.reason: Each part pads itself, so Body's scroll box holds its own padding and focus rings inside it are not clipped.

border-width.reason: No border-width token scale exists (#154); every module uses a literal width.

display.reason: Stacks Header, Body and Actions, each padding itself; the native closed dialog stays display:none.

position.reason: Overrides the native absolute positioning so the non-modal dialog takes its place in the page flow.

margin.reason: Overrides the native auto margins that centre a dialog.

max-width.reason: Fits its container in the page flow.

padding-block-end.reason: When Body renders (description or children set) it is the last part and pads its own bottom, inside its scroll box.

min-height.reason: Lets the flex child shrink so it scrolls instead of overflowing the dialog.

overflow-y.reason: Long content scrolls inside Body; Header and Actions stay visible.

overscroll-behavior.reason: Scrolling past the end of Body doesn't scroll the page behind the dialog.

sets.name: Dialog
sets.covers: The modal dialog surface: one component with Title, Has description + Description, Has children + Children slot (both inside the Body frame), Has actions + Actions slot (preferred: Button, TextLink). Page Dialog; examples in section 3043:8290.

divergences.what: Close is an absolutely positioned layer 12px from the top and right edges, and Header has 40px right padding, instead of an in-flow button with a negative inline-end margin.
divergences.decision: Accepted: Figma auto layout has no per-child negative margin. The glyph lands 20px from the top and right edges and the title wraps at the same width, as in code.

divergences.what: Root carries the inline padding (space/inset/lg) and an item spacing of space/stack/md; Actions pads its top by space/stack/sm. Code pads each part and Root only on the block axis.
divergences.decision: Accepted: the code split exists so Body's scroll box holds its own padding (focus rings); Figma doesn't scroll. Spacing between parts is identical.

divergences.what: Root's top padding is bound to space/inset/sm (12px); code computes calc(space.inset.lg - space.inset.xs).
divergences.decision: Accepted: Figma can't bind a calc. Same value; rebind if either token changes.

divergences.what: The Body part's slot layer is named Children, and children is paired with a Has children boolean.
divergences.decision: Accepted: a Figma slot layer and its property share one name, and ADR-026 names the default slot Children. An empty slot still takes a gap, so it needs an on/off property like Description and Actions.
divergences.notes: Same naming as Card's Children slot. The gap comes from auto layout.

divergences.what: The Body frame (Description + Children slot) stays in the layout when both Has description and Has children are off, adding one space/stack/md gap (82px tall instead of 66px).
divergences.decision: Accepted: Figma can't hide a frame on either of two booleans. Only a title-and-actions-only dialog is affected; no pattern draws one.

divergences.what: Title sits in a wrapper frame padded by size/025 (2px) top and bottom.
divergences.decision: Accepted: Figma's Subheader line is 28px, so 2px brings it to the 32px Close height and centres the x on the first line, which code computes from font.size.subheader and font.line-height.default.

decisions.decision: The description sits at the top of `Body`, above your content. `Header` holds only the title and the close button.
decisions.reason: Placed on its own between the header and the body, the description looked detached. MUI's dialogs put it inside the content the same way.
decisions.notes: Found in visual review 2026-11-16. Body renders when description or children is set, and the description scrolls with the content. Description pads its bottom by space.stack.md only when content follows it, so consumer children keep their own layout (no gap on Body).

decisions.decision: Each section (`Header`, `Body`, `Actions`) has its own padding. The dialog itself pads only the top and bottom.
decisions.reason: `Body` scrolls, which clips anything outside its box. With the padding on the dialog, a focused field at the edge of `Body` lost its focus ring.
decisions.notes: Found in visual review 2026-11-16. Body pads all four sides inside its scroll box. Section-owned padding is how MUI's DialogContent works; padding plus a cancelling negative margin was rejected as a workaround. Spacing between parts is unchanged: when Body is the last part, Root drops its bottom padding and Body pads space.inset.lg instead.

decisions.reason: Our buttons have borders or fills, and the 4px focus ring took half of an 8px gap, so a focused button nearly touched the next one.
decisions.notes: MUI uses 8px, but its default actions are borderless text buttons. Found in visual review 2026-11-16.

decisions.decision: The close button lines up with the content edge and sits centred on the title's first line, however many lines the title wraps to.
decisions.reason: A small round button has padding around its icon, so without an offset the × sits inside the content edge and above the title text.
decisions.notes: Original entry, kept for the mechanics: Close is pulled right by space.inset.xs so its glyph lines up with the content edge, and Root's top padding is reduced by the same amount. Title pads its block axis so its first line is as tall as Close (size.400), and Header aligns to the start. An sm round Button is size.400 with an sm icon, leaving space.inset.xs of transparent padding around the glyph; without the right offset the x sits that far inside the Header padding (visual review 2026-11-16). This is MUI IconButton's edge technique, and it keeps the hit target. Aligning box tops left the x 6px above the title text because of Title's half-leading. Padding Title to the button's height (Primer's Dialog header) centres the x on the first line however many lines the title wraps to, which align-items: center would not, and needs no vertical negative margin. Root's top padding is space.inset.xs shorter than its other sides, so the x glyph sits space.inset.lg from both the top and right edges. It assumes Close stays size sm and Title stays size subheader; changing either means changing these values.

decisions.decision: Dialog sets its own role, name and open state. Passing `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `title`, `open`, `onCancel` or `onClose` is a type error.
decisions.reason: Dialog names itself from `title` and listens to the cancel and close events to keep the `open` prop in sync.
decisions.notes: Omitted from the native <dialog> attributes in the props type; @ts-expect-error cases in the a11y test. Applies the packages/components AGENTS.md type-enforced anti-pattern rule.

decisions.decision: Built on the native `<dialog>` element, not a `div` with a JavaScript focus trap.
decisions.reason: The browser blocks the rest of the page, handles Escape and draws the dialog above everything, with no z-index. Every major browser has supported this since 2023.
decisions.notes: showModal() gives an inert background (keyboard, pointer and screen reader), Escape as a cancel event and the top layer (no z-index token needed). showModal() supported since 2022, inert since 2023.

decisions.decision: Focus stays in the dialog because the page behind it is blocked, not because Tab wraps around. Tab past the last control may reach the browser's own controls before coming back.
decisions.reason: This meets WCAG's rules on focus order and keyboard traps (2.4.3, 2.1.2). Wrap-around advice was written for dialogs built from a `div`.
decisions.notes: Also WCAG 2.4.11 (focus not obscured). APG's wrap-around guidance predates native <dialog>. Reviewers should not flag the missing wrap.

decisions.decision: On open, focus goes to the first element marked `data-autofocus`, or else to the title.
decisions.reason: React's `autoFocus` doesn't work here, so the marker lets you choose, for example Cancel in a destructive confirm. Focusing the title announces the dialog first.
decisions.notes: React 18 never writes autoFocus into the DOM: it calls focus() at mount, before Dialog's effect opens the dialog, so the call is lost and the native focusing steps find no autofocus attribute. Cancel first in a destructive confirm per APG. Title (tabIndex -1) as the default announces the dialog's name and description and keeps Enter from closing it, which focusing Close first would do.

decisions.decision: On close, focus returns to the element that opened the dialog, if it still exists and you haven't moved focus yourself.
decisions.reason: The opener may be gone (a menu item closes with its menu), and you may want focus somewhere else, such as the menu button.
decisions.notes: Original entry, kept for the exact conditions: Focus returns to the element focused before opening, only when that element is still connected and focus is still in the dialog or on the body. When that element is gone, focus left inside the closed dialog is blurred to the body. A menu item that opened the dialog is gone by the time it closes (DropdownMenu closes on select). The condition lets the consumer move focus in onOpenChange(false) (for example to the menu button) without Dialog taking it back.

decisions.decision: The `open` prop decides whether the dialog is open. Escape asks to close through `onOpenChange(false)`, and if the browser closes the dialog itself, the prop is updated to match.
decisions.reason: One source of truth keeps your state and the dialog from disagreeing.
decisions.notes: Original entry, kept for the event mechanics: Modal Escape is handled through the cancel event with preventDefault; non-modal Escape through keydown. A close event calls onOpenChange(false) only when the open prop is true and the element is closed at the time the event arrives. Keeps the open prop the single source of truth. Browsers may close a modal dialog on a repeated Escape even when cancel is prevented (close-request anti-abuse); the close listener resyncs the prop when that happens. close is queued as a task, so one fired by the effect cleanup can arrive after the effect reopened the dialog (StrictMode, Fast Refresh, toggling nonModal while open); checking the element's own open state ignores it.

decisions.decision: When the title gets focus after a keyboard open, it shows the standard focus ring. After a mouse open, it doesn't.
decisions.reason: Keyboard users need to see where focus landed, and the focus ring is never replaced.
decisions.notes: ADR-028 forbids replacing the ring; menu items are the only exception and Title is not one. The screenshot baseline shows the ring on purpose (headless capture has no prior interaction).

decisions.decision: `Body` isn't made focusable when it scrolls. In Safari, a long `Body` of plain text can't be scrolled with the keyboard.
decisions.reason: Making it focusable would add a Tab stop and a landmark to every long dialog, for one browser.
decisions.notes: Chrome 130+ and Firefox make scroll containers focusable; Safari does not. The rejected fix is tabIndex plus a region role. Revisit if Safari users report it or axe's scrollable-region-focusable flags a real page.

decisions.decision: The backdrop colour comes from a CSS custom property read inside `::backdrop`.
decisions.reason: Current browsers pass custom properties to the backdrop. Older ones show the browser's default backdrop, which still dims the page.
decisions.notes: ::backdrop inherits from its dialog in Chrome 122, Firefox 120 and Safari 17.4.

decisions.decision: The shadow reuses Card's elevated shadow.
decisions.reason: There's no shadow token scale yet. One shared shadow keeps Card and Dialog consistent until there is.
The browser centres a dialog with its own `margin: auto`, and the CSS reset removes it, which pins the dialog to the top-left corner.
decisions.notes: Caught in the first screenshot baseline, not by any test.

ruledOut.option: A JavaScript focus trap (trapFocus / disableEnforceFocus props)
ruledOut.reason: showModal() inertness already contains focus, for screen readers too, with no trap code to maintain.
No component forwards a ref (#114), so a ref prop would only work on raw elements. data-autofocus and the conditional return cover the known cases.

ruledOut.option: Focusing the <dialog> element itself on open
ruledOut.reason: The global :focus-visible ring would outline the whole panel, and removing it needs an ADR-028 exception. Title takes the same role with a small ring.

ruledOut.option: A modal prop defaulting to true
ruledOut.reason: ADR-026 booleans default to false, so the flag names the less common case (nonModal). modal=true would need a vocabulary waiver like Inline's wrap.
A stray click would discard a half-filled form. Escape and Close are enough until a consumer needs light dismiss.

ruledOut.option: Locking page scroll while the modal is open
ruledOut.reason: It needs a global style or an inline style on <html>, which component modules can't own. Body uses overscroll-behavior: contain instead.
One width (size.dialog.max) serves both known consumers; add an axis when a page needs a second width.
It only stops a later mouse click on the title text from focusing it and drawing the ring. Cosmetic, and it adds a blur handler to keep in sync with initial focus.
